verification.note: Fresh Cambridge open-access PDF downloaded; selected1–15 including substantive sections and notes1–73 read, visual4. Joint scholarly mediation explicitly retained.4/n20 quotes Porter’s1997 Lancet interview on Thompson; that interview and full1985 Patient’s View not independently read.11–14 both criticise methodological gaps in Porter’s practice and defend productive extensions; do not collapse criticism of later followers into criticism of Porter. Later2016 retrospective cannot be an original formative source. Foucault translations differentiated5/n24.

roy_porter_lay_1985.note: Fresh Cambridge publisher PDF downloaded 2026-10-28; selected printed138–143 and162–165, including notes1–20/143–149, read anew; visual139/163. This extends the old opening-only reading, not a claim to complete reading of all31pages. Own139 explicitly praises Annales perspectives and Foucault/Ariès on biomedical beliefs;163/n147 uses Burke against rigid cultural strata,164 endorses Jewson. Concluding165 restricts the magazine to one social sector and explicitly one sex; disappearance of medicine from its pages does not end lay medical culture. Original cited books remain unread here.
